To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supplementation with DFM, XA, and XAP increased growth performance, nutrient digestion, and reduced the ileal flow of NSP in broilers.
DFM+XAp improved performance and nutrient digestibility compared with CTL and DFM+XA, and reduced numbers of Camplylobacter and Bacteroidaceae spp in cecal content.
the DFM+XPA combination had a greater than expected additive effect on BW, BWG (d 22‐42) and FI (d 22 ‐42) compared with the DFM or XPA treatments alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the efficacy of a multi‐strain DFM and two enzyme combinations on broiler performance, NSP digestibility, gut microbial composition and nutrient digestibility.
the efficacy of two multi‐enzyme combinations and a probiotic on growth, nutrient digestibility and gut microbial populations in broilers.

the effects of a multi‐strain probiotic (DFMs) alone or in combination with multi‐enzyme combinations (XAs and XAPs) on growth, nutrient and energy digestibility and disappearance of NSP and gut microbial populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of a multi‐strain DFM and protease to the diets of broilers improved growth performance, digestibilities of energy and nutrients and disappearance of NSP, and reduced numbers of Camplobacter and Bacteroidetes in the cecae.
DFM supplementation increased BWG and FI, whereas XA and XA+DF improved AMEn.
supplementation with DFM and XAP increased growth performance and nutrient digestibility, decreased NSP flow to the hindgut, and reduced Campylobacter and Bacteroidetes in the cecums of broilers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DFM supplementation increased BW and BWG and improved nutrient digestibility and NSP disappearance.

the DFM alone had beneficial effects on performance and NSP digestibility and XA and XA+DF had beneficial effects on NSP digestibility, but that the combination of DFM and XA had additive effects on performance and XAP+DFM had additive effects on AIDE and performance, with the protease component being critical for the beneficial effects of XAP+DF on performance and NSPs.
supplementation of DFM+XPA resulted in the greatest improvement in growth, energy and nutrient digestibility, and disappearance of NSP, with the addition of XA to DFM+Xap having an additive effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inclusion of DFM and protease in the diet can have additive and synergistic effects on growth performance and energy and nutrient digestibility, and that the protease may play a key role in increasing the digestibility of NSP.
the combination of a Bacillus probiotics with a multi‐enzyme combination can have a greater than additive benefit on broiler performance, digestibility, and disappearance of NSP.

the inclusion of a DFM and a multi‐enzyme combination containing a protease can have a beneficial effect on broiler growth performance and nutrient digestibility, and can also reduce numbers of Campylocbacter spp. in the cecums of broilers.
